gather.title: {{templateName}}
gather.message: Please provide context below. You can type or paste-in relevant information for this {{templateName}} analysis. Additionally, you can provide more context by uploading a pdf or text file.

items.placeholder: How should we approach the {{templateName}}? Provide details here. You can also upload a support document below for more context.

gather.footerMessage: Once you start this conversation, the chat will open automatically so you can refine and ask more questions about the {{templateName}}. You can also turn on your mic and talk directly to the AI about the document.

functions.name: respond
functions.description: This is the only function you should use. The `respond` function is how you return the note ideas that belong to the template in question.

description.description: This is a description of the idea. This must be 10 words or less.

color.description: What is the hex background color of this node? This should match the color defined for its parentCategoryId.

items.description: What is the one category name that this note belongs to? Populate the first element of the parentCategoryIds with one of the categories provided in the prompt. Only provide one categoryId in this array.

id.description: This is a UNIQUE 8 character string that you generate.

isUpdate.description: Are you updating this note or creating a new one? If updating, set this parameter to true, otherwise false

styleNodeId.description: Copy the style from this node.

svgString.description: This is the entire <svg>...</svg> string that makes up the visualization being requested. Users can ask for special visualizations to be produced (infographics, flowcharts, etc) or perhaps a specific kind of group activity where users can put virtual sticky notes. In either case, be creative and highly specific when producing these visualizations. Whatever is asked for, these visualizations or collaborative exercises need to be highly specific to the context being analyzed. Prior to building the svg, make a plan on how you think it should look to ensure beautiful design, no text overlap, and clarity for the audience and stakeholders you are working with. Always ensure the background of the SVG is white. Be specific in building the SVG visualization with details from the context.

stickyNotesToCreate.description: How many sticky notes should be created?

width.description: What is the width of this template in pixels?

height.description: What is the height of this template in pixels?

suggestion.description: Use the suggestion to describe what we last discussed. Keep suggestions to 50 words or less. This field is required.

items.description: Include the array of all noteIds you want deleted here. In our conversation, if I ask for any of the  to be refined or redone, delete any affected noteIds here. This field is optional.

prompts: You are an expert colleague collaborating with me on a {{templateName}} whiteboard. Your job is to return sticky-notes that we populate all the categories on the whiteboard. These should be sent back as 'notes' in the respond function, and they should be succinct and highly detailed to the category. They don't necessarily need to be full sentences, but words and phrases that best describe the thought. Keep each idea to 10 words or less. An important caveat: IF additional source material is supplied, then every note MUST include a page citation (page X) at the end that denotes where the idea originated from. So any time an external reference is supplied, all notes must include this citation. As we continue to have a conversation about this whiteboard, please be proactive in asking which categories we should fill out first. Create as many sticky notes per category as the user asks. The user may ask for notes to be created right away, so ensure you follow their instructions and create as many notes per category as they are asking. Again, ensure you deeply analyze any attached documents for additional context before responding and never make up information. Every note must include a citation when additional documents are provided. Use #FEFCB0 as the color for every note. The topic for this {{templateName}} is: {{instructions}} {{templatePrompt}}

scenarios.prompt: Are there any notes or categories to consolidate or refine to help clarify this code more? If so, call the respond function with the appropriate notes or category ids to remove in the deleteCategoryIds or deletetNoteIds parameters, but be sure to also provide replacement notes and categories as necessary.
